text:
Ty Dellandrea was the 13th pick of the 2018 draft, and at 26 he's a checking forward in San Jose still looking for an offensive game. He has one assist in 11 games and 35 hits, and his minutes have dropped by more than a minute a night lately. Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest noted one game where his shift ended early in a period, unsure whether it was a benching or an injury.

The five-on-five numbers are tough: the Sharks have taken 35% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about nine points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey's numbers last season said offense isn't his game, and his "plays like" list (Nic Dowd, Tanner Jeannot, Adam Lowry) tells you what kind of role he's meant to fill.

The problem is that those players win their minutes, and Dellandrea hasn't yet. Our range says 4 to 12 goals over a full season. On a rebuilding team with young forwards pushing for ice time, the next month decides whether he holds a regular spot.
headline: Dellandrea's spot is under pressure
